reason: Training-emulation idea is attractive and single-GPU-flavoured, but no artifact link, CRIU/cuda-checkpoint privilege risk, and fidelity is only validated against inaccessible production clusters.
Classic learned/statistical cardinality estimator inside a query optimizer: CPU-only and runnable, but far from OS resource management.
MLIR sub-operator compiler with a dedicated reproducibility repo; CPU-only and buildable, but a data-systems compiler rather than an OS topic.
Pure user-space verifier/sandbox runtime needing no root or counters, but a patched-LLVM build and no artifact evaluation, and determinism enforcement is only adjacent to resource management.
Microservice load-shifting policy is squarely a scheduling topic but no official repo was found and the evaluation targets a large shared cluster.
Single-Ampere-GPU sparse kernels fit the machine directly with a public repo, but it is GNN kernel engineering rather than systems resource management.
Paged-CSR plus delta-page storage engine is real storage-engine design with an open repo; completeness of the artifact is unknown and extensions are moderately deep.
Plain-C trace-driven OPT/page-replacement simulator comparable to libCacheSim runs entirely in user space; only caveats are a 72-core baseline and a repo idle since 2024.
Retrieval-augmented LLM compiler-optimization pipeline: CPU-side and buildable, but LLM-for-compilers work with uncertain model/API dependencies and little OS content.

Checkpoint I/O, serialization and resharding are genuine storage problems and the repo is a pip-installable library with tests; headline numbers need thousands of GPUs so only the single-node path is reproducible.
Latency-predictor study fits one GPU easily but is measured by prediction accuracy, not system performance, and the paper's repo URL is stale.
Chunked-prefill LLM scheduling is the canonical KV-cache/scheduling target, pure user-space Python on vLLM, and a 7B model on 24 GB is a natural scale-down with many policy knobs to extend.
Offline trace-driven placement oracle runs on one machine, but the artifact is Docker-first and cloud-cost optimization is only adjacent to OS resource management.
Deep-learning estimator for LIKE predicates: fits the machine but is an ML-modelling contribution inside the optimizer with a narrow extension space.
User-space io_uring NVMe engine in LeanStore needs no root and the machine has real NVMe; only absolute IOPS scale down from 8 SSDs to 2, and the io branch gives a concrete base to extend.
Learned lifetime-aware GC for KV-separated LSM on RocksDB is single-node, disk-bound and highly on-topic; artifact completeness of the fork is unverified.
SGMV kernel plus multi-tenant batching works on one Ampere GPU with a public repo; the scheduler evaluation used a small cluster so scale-down is to one base model with many adapters.
Zenodo artifact and interference reproducible with co-located processes, but configuration auto-tuning under noise is adjacent to, not core, OS resource management.
Learned prefetching touches caching/prefetch policy and runs on one node, but the note is thin about artifact completeness and it is a database-workload-specific learned component.
Model checking for Kubernetes controllers is user-space and has a clean state-space-reduction performance target, but it is verification tooling with only an Available badge.
DL cluster scheduling policy studied through a bundled simulator driven by measured throughput tables, so the 64-GPU cluster is not needed; the Docker-first AE path and repo renaming add friction.
GPU join/aggregation operators run fine on one 24 GB card but this is query-operator engineering rather than an OS resource-management problem.
A drop-in user-space dynamic loader with Available+Functional+Reproduced badges on the exact Debian family of this machine; only the VM-image convenience path is unusable without KVM.
CPU-only SIMD/cache-conscious ANN index would run here, but no repository is linked in the batch and ANN indexing is not an OS topic.
Evaluated on an A4000, so our A5000 is comfortable and out-of-core GPU data movement is systems-flavoured; the CUDA >= 12.4 requirement against driver 535 is a real build risk.
Geometric-deep-learning cardinality estimator with a PostgreSQL harness: runnable but an ML-modelling contribution with limited systems headroom.
Deduplication in Ceph is ideal storage material and is merged upstream, but building Ceph without root or apt is a severe feasibility risk for a 10-week project.
README-confirmed CUDA 11.8 / single-GPU setup with pretrained weights makes it trivially runnable, but point-cloud DNN acceleration is a domain ML-systems topic.
Sketch-based working-set-size estimation and adaptive cache sizing is exactly the caching topic, AE Reproduced, and the standalone trace-driven estimator avoids the JVM/Alluxio multi-node parts.
Memory-footprint-driven in-memory index for key-value stores runs entirely in user space on commodity x86; artifact completeness unknown and the design space is fairly closed.
CPU-only trace-driven simulator with a crisp quantitative objective, but privacy budgeting is only a systems topic through the catch-all category.

Unified sparse attention for long-context serving is core KV-cache work and Llama-3-8B fits 24 GB, but the longest-context configs assume 40-80 GB GPUs and the code lives inside the larger OmniServe repo.
No code release found, federated participants must be serialized on one GPU, and MoE federated fine-tuning is an ML-training topic rather than OS resource management.
Model-file dedup/compression is genuine storage work that fits in 257 GB, but a measurement study gives a narrower improvement axis and needs tens of GB of downloads.
Single-V100 reference hardware means the A5000 is fine and the artifact is complete, but the AE asks for 256 GB RAM for the big graphs and we have ~111 GB, forcing smaller datasets.
Attention-based cardinality estimator wired into PostgreSQL fits one node, but it is an optimizer-ML contribution with modest systems headroom.

Freeze-aware memory management inside JVM/Node runtimes is core user-space memory/GC work exercisable with cgroup v2 limits, but the FaaS harness likely assumes containers and a runtime source build is heavy.
Portable auto-vectorizing C++ columnar format with cascading encodings runs CPU-only on one node and leaves obvious encoding/heuristic knobs to extend.
A buffer manager that deliberately avoids kernel modules would be an ideal user-space memory-management target, but no repository could be located, which is disqualifying under the hard requirement.
User-space Rust Datalog engine builds here, but incremental recursive query evaluation is a language/data-systems topic rather than OS resource management.
Prefix-aware decode attention is KV-cache-adjacent CUDA/Triton work that runs on one Ampere GPU with a Zenodo AE artifact; kernel-level projects need solid GPU skills but scale down cleanly.

ChampSim is CPU-only and trace-driven so the whole simulation study reproduces here and prefetch policies are easy to vary; it is microarchitectural prefetching, not OS-level management, and the RTL analysis is out of reach.
CPU-only, modest-memory ANN index that runs easily here, but range-filtering vector search is not an OS resource-management problem.
Hybrid column-row cloud storage engine is on-topic storage work, but the object-store experiments need a MinIO substitute and the Umbra-derived codebase may be hard to build.
LSM compaction policy for space amplification is textbook storage work, single node and JVM-based, with an obvious space of policy variants; artifact completeness is unverified.
Heterogeneous LoRA batching and adapter orchestration on LightLLM is on-topic serving work and LLaVA-7B fits, but A100-tuned tiling kernels need SM86 retuning and adapters must be fine-tuned first.
CPU-only range filter evaluated inside key-value workloads is directly relevant to storage engines, cheap to run, and filter design offers clear testable variants.

LazyFS is a FUSE file system and /dev/fuse plus setuid fusermount3 make it run unprivileged here; it is crash-consistency testing tooling, so improvements are about fault-search efficiency rather than performance.
Multi-JVM targets fit in 125 GiB and the efficiency metric is measurable, but this is debugging/testing tooling with long experiment runs, not resource management.
CPU-only multicore mining engine fits the machine, but hypergraph pattern mining is an algorithms/compiler topic and the large datasets need checking.
Serverless scaling policies evaluated against public production traces is exactly the trace-driven scheduling work this machine supports, with both artifact and traces released.
Predictive GPU scheduling would be a strong topic and simulatable from traces, but no code was found and the target is a multi-tenant cluster.
Compaction-as-resource-investment is ideal single-machine storage material with rich policy headroom, but no official repository was located.
Full code for a single-node RocksDB join/secondary-index benchmark makes reproduction easy, but a systematic benchmark offers a narrower improvement axis than a mechanism paper.
Dafny proof-automation tooling runs fine on CPU but has essentially no OS resource-management content and improvements would be proof-engineering.
Tensor-relational rewriting is a compiler/query-engine contribution targeting large-scale sparse tensors that must be scaled down, with unknown artifact completeness.

The offline time-energy Pareto planner is a graph algorithm improvable from profiles and NVML needs no root, but end-to-end validation needs pipeline-parallel multi-GPU training and frequency locking may require privileges.
Small neural models replacing range-aggregate queries fit the GPU easily, but this is a learned approximation technique with little systems substance to extend.
Resilient-step runtime is an interesting user-space abstraction, but no artifact is confirmed and the evaluation is a distributed cloud service requiring a substantial scale-down.
Wasm-embedded decoders in a columnar format are pure user-space storage/compression work on one node with clear extension points; artifact maturity of a very recent repo is unverified.
Tensor-level dedup and delta quantization is compression/storage-engine work that fits one node, with obvious knobs (chunking, quantization levels) to vary; repo completeness unknown.

Online-learning resource allocation is an excellent OS topic and pure Python, but every released experiment assumes Kubernetes/EKS with Docker, so a trace-driven simulator would have to be written from scratch.

Iteration-level preemptive MLFQ scheduling plus KV swapping is exactly the LLM-serving scheduling topic and a 7-8B model fits, but the custom C++ engine and distributed baseline make reproduction heavier than a vLLM-based system.
Request scheduling over a hybrid KV/hidden cache is directly on-topic and single-GPU friendly; the note gives no evidence about artifact completeness.
CPU-only compiler IR evaluated on desktop-class x86 reproduces trivially here, but tensor-contraction layout optimization is a compiler topic with little OS content.
The LLVM static-analysis core runs unprivileged, but the mount-based validation plugins need root, so a project is confined to analysis precision on file-system source code.
Predicate transfer in DuckDB runs entirely in user space on one node with public code, but join-order robustness is a query-processing topic.
CPU-GPU cooperative scheduling of the preprocessing pipeline is real resource management with a natural single-GPU path, but multi-GPU results are unreproducible and artifact maturity is unknown.
KV-cache reuse as a vLLM 0.8.5 extension is pure user space on one GPU with FlashAttention-2 support on Ampere; only the 70B A100 configs are out of reach.

Flash-cache admission/eviction co-designed with GC is a great caching topic, but the WREN/FDP interface needs special SSD support and root, leaving only a simulation-based study on an unofficial CacheLib fork.
Coroutine-based prefetching targeting cache misses is memory-hierarchy-flavoured and CPU-only, but it is a graph-processing engine and artifact completeness is unverified.
Chunk-level KV-cache reuse for RAG is squarely the core topic and 7B models fit one GPU, but no official repository is linked, which blocks the hard requirement.
Clock-based intra-kernel instrumentation avoids perf and root, but the motivating warp-specialized Hopper use case may be inapplicable on SM86 and Triton needs a conda CUDA 12.x toolchain.

Token-granularity multiplexing of many models onto one GPU is inherently single-GPU and the paper has a single-A10 experiment, but the AE expects H100 nodes, 512 GB RAM and 256 GB of weights so a serious scale-down is mandatory.

Deliberately counter-free GPU profiling sidesteps perf_event_paranoid and the artifact is Available+Functional+Reproduced; SASS probing is driver/arch sensitive and profiling is observability rather than resource management.
DBI-based value profiling needs no root or counters and has GitHub plus Zenodo artifacts, but it is profiling tooling and DBI frameworks are finicky to build.
Single-GPU random-walk engine fits the card, but graph sampling is a domain workload rather than an OS resource-management problem.
User-space static analyzer runs here easily, but it predicts cloud API costs rather than managing resources and the only improvement axis is analysis precision.
Single-GPU approximate model invocation for point-cloud queries fits the machine but is an ML-in-DB application with little systems-resource content.

An NVMe-backed second JVM heap to cut GC pressure is core user-space memory management with GitHub plus Zenodo artifacts; the OpenJDK source build and Spark/Giraph harness make it a heavy but single-node effort.
